- **Status:** Ready (Decider D86: its backlog starts with the Tasks app of card 135, which is growth checkpoint one)
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** data (thin slice; a backlog and a pre-registration Decider)
- **Milestone:** Codebase size: does Phrase's cost fall and its edge widen as the codebase grows?
- **Source:** Steve's answers relayed by Dispatch, 2026-10-27 (use a publicly available repository instead of his private projects, and optionally a growth study) and Decider D84 (Codex Yes; Grok Support-it; Copilot out of quota). Separate from the frozen bar (D32); nothing is re-scored. The private projects play-tracker and BaccaratSim are dropped and are never snapshotted, opened or referenced.
- **Depends on:** 120
- **Story:** As Steve, I want an ordered feature backlog with specs written up front and a pre-registered plan for growing two projects feature by feature, so that cost and pass rate can be read as a curve against codebase size without contamination.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a new invented application (a multi-endpoint service), When the backlog is written, Then it is an ordered list of features of one difficulty class, each with its Given/When/Then specs and outcome cases written before any run, expressible in the language that already compiles, with a hash of the backlog and specs recorded
  2. Given the plan, When the Decider runs, Then it records the paired checkpoints at named sizes on the 1, 10 and 50 endpoint grid (both arms grow from the same checkpoint at each size to limit path dependence), N independent runs per arm with seeds, the models and versions, the dated price snapshot, the exclusion rules, a pass definition (the feature specs and the full regression pass) and a success sentence, before any row
  3. Given the record, When the run card starts, Then a check fails if the Decider is missing or dated after the first row

## Context

- Uses the token, attempt, timeout and dollar definitions of the frozen bar and D81 and changes no frozen number. Cost is higher than one-shot tasks: sizes and N are chosen with the allotments in mind.
